hero.lede: Impulse blocks the apps and websites that steal your focus — so you reclaim 2+ hours every day. No willpower required.

problem.label: The problem
problem.title: Your attention is being sold.
problem.body: Every feed is a slot machine. The scroll never ends because it was never meant to. You’re not fighting a habit — you’re fighting an industry of designers paid to keep you there.

manifesto.label: Why we built this
manifesto.quoteBefore: We don’t think all screen time is bad. We think
manifesto.body: Impulse helps you be intentional — not through guilt or rules, but by giving you control over the impulse, not the dopamine.

features.label: Features
features.title: Everything you need to take back control.

blocks.title: Blocks that can’t be paused.
blocks.body: Create profiles like Work, Study or Bedtime, each with its own sites and schedule. Strict blocks can’t be bypassed or paused: they end when they end.
blocks.check2: and focus runs on its own, with nothing left to touch.

limits.title: Not just how long. How many times.
limits.body: Give YouTube 30 minutes a day. Give Instagram 5 openings. Capping how often you open an app cuts the automatic reach far earlier than capping the minutes does.
limits.check1: in minutes, per site or per app.
limits.check2: the limit almost nobody else offers.

mobile.title: We stop you right before the scroll.
mobile.body: Before letting you into an app we show you how long you’ve been on it today and how many times you’ve already tried. Usually, seeing it is enough to close it.
mobile.check1: in front of you, at the exact moment it matters.
mobile.check2: The number no other app shows you.

stats.title: See where your time actually goes.
stats.body: Today’s screen time, openings, blocks kept and the apps eating the most of it. No lecturing: just the numbers you need to decide what to change.
stats.check1: so you see the pattern, not just the total.
stats.check2Strong: It all stays on your device.

bridge.label: Desktop and mobile
bridge.title: Most blockers stop at your phone. Ours doesn’t.
bridge.body1: Distraction just hops to the laptop. So Impulse is also a Chrome and Safari extension, with its own blocker for the computer that works without your phone in front of you.
bridge.body2: And the bridge between them? Your phone. Tap it against your Disc or any NFC tag and the desktop block lifts. The off-switch stops living on the same screen as the temptation.
bridge.check1: Set it up on the computer; no phone required.
bridge.check2: You stay on the tab you’re on and everything else goes quiet.
bridge.check3Strong: Unlock the computer with your phone.
bridge.check3: One NFC tap ends a desktop blocking period.
bridge.check4Strong: And soon, a native macOS app,

items.title: Free to start, no account
items.body: Download and start blocking in seconds. No sign-up wall, no credit card.

items.title: Built for real life
items.body: Emergency access, gentle modes and groups — strict, but never cruel.

items.a: Yes. The core blocker is 100% free on iPhone, Android and Chrome, with no account and no credit card. Scheduled blocks, Quick Focus and screen-time insights cost nothing. Impulse Pro adds unlimited rules, strict mode and Focus Groups for those who want more, but you can take back hours every day without paying a cent.

items.q: How is Impulse different from other focus apps?
items.a: Three things. It works on both your phone and your browser, so distraction can’t just hop to your laptop. It has strictness levels you genuinely can’t bypass in a weak moment, up to a physical tap. And it never guilt-trips you: it blocks what you choose, when you choose, then gets out of the way.

items.q: How does Impulse block apps and websites on iPhone?
items.a: On iOS, Impulse uses Apple’s Screen Time API — the same secure framework Apple built for this. On the desktop it runs as a Chrome and Safari extension. You create profiles, pick what to block, then activate on a schedule, on demand with Quick Focus, or under a strict unlock.

items.q: What if I have a real emergency?
items.a: Impulse is strict, not cruel. Emergency unlocks let you reach what you genuinely need, but they’re intentionally inconvenient, and blocks reactivate automatically afterwards, so one exception never quietly becomes a relapse.

Completely. Your usage stats and block lists stay on your device, not on our servers. No tracking, no ads, no selling your data to anyone. Your attention is the product everyone else is trying to sell. Not here.

items.q: Does it work on Android and on my computer?
items.a: Yes. Impulse runs on iPhone and Android, plus Chrome and Safari on the desktop. The native macOS app is on the way.

finalCta.lede: Join 1,000+ people reclaiming 2 hours a day. Free on iPhone, Android and your browser — start in under a minute.

how.label: How it works
how.title: A physical barrier between you and the scroll.

steps.title: Pick what to block, and how hard
steps.body: Create profiles like Work, Study or Bedtime, each with its own apps, schedule and unlock level. Set the level to Physical and your Disc becomes the only key.

steps.title: Tap your Disc to start
steps.body: One tap and the focus session begins. Not nearby? Start it straight from the app instead.

steps.title: Put distance between you and the Disc
steps.body: Leave it in another room, a drawer, by the front door. That physical separation turns unblocking into a conscious choice, and quietly breaks the habit loop.

steps.title: Come back with purpose
steps.body: When you’re truly done, tap again to unblock. Need an unexpected exception? Emergency unlocks live in the app, but they’re intentionally inconvenient.

compare.label: How we compare
compare.title: Open by design.
compare.lede: Most physical blockers sell you a gadget and lock you in. We give you the friction either way — and it already works on your phone and your browser.
